Get the selection table from a sweep

Source: R/sweep.R
selection_table.Rd

Returns the table of fitted candidates from a sweep_models() result, sorted by AIC (lowest first).

Usage

selection_table(x, converged_only = TRUE)

Arguments

x

A dsfit_sweep object from sweep_models().

converged_only

Logical. TRUE (default) drops candidates that failed to fit or did not converge.

Value

A tibble with one row per candidate and columns:

model_id, key, adjustment, order, formula

The candidate, as in model_set().

converged

TRUE if the fit succeeded.

n_par

Number of estimated parameters.

aic, delta_aic

AIC, and its difference from the lowest AIC.

p, p_se, p_cv

Average detection probability over the searched strip, its standard error, and its coefficient of variation.

esw

Effective strip half-width: p times the width of the searched strip (truncation minus left).

cvm_p

Cramer-von Mises goodness-of-fit p-value. NA for binned distances.

chisq_p

Chi-square goodness-of-fit p-value. The test to read for binned distances.

Columns describing a fit are NA for a candidate that failed.

See also

sweep_models()

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(object = 1:150, distance = abs(rnorm(150, 0, 100)))
d <- d[d$distance < 300, ]
selection_table(sweep_models(d, truncation = 300, quiet = TRUE))
#> # A tibble: 2 × 15
#>   model_id key   adjustment order formula converged n_par   aic delta_aic     p
#>   <chr>    <chr> <chr>      <int> <chr>   <lgl>     <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 hn       hn    NA            NA ~1      TRUE          1 1570.      0    0.378
#> 2 hr       hr    NA            NA ~1      TRUE          2 1574.      4.47 0.388
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: p_se <dbl>, p_cv <dbl>, esw <dbl>, cvm_p <dbl>,
#> #   chisq_p <dbl>
